writeup.headline: Qualcomm rates Hold: strong margins and balance sheet offset by weak growth and middling valuation.
writeup.thesis: Qualcomm scores 56, a Hold, because solid quality and balance-sheet scores are held back by a weak growth score. Growth scores 28: TTM revenue growth of 1.9%, a latest-quarter revenue decline of 4.0% year on year, and growth slowed by 0.6 pp from the previous quarter. Quality scores 76, with a 54.2% gross margin, a 23.2% operating margin, a 23.6% FCF margin and diluted share count down 2.7% year on year. The balance sheet scores 79, with net debt at 0.48 times FCF. Valuation scores 52: in absolute terms P/S of 4.4x, P/FCF of 18.4x and EV/EBIT of 19.3x are moderate, with the FCF yield 0.4 pp above the 10-year Treasury yield. Against its own history the stock is near the middle overall, though EV/EBIT is more expensive than at 43 of the last 61 month-ends. Trend (55) and news (59) are neutral to mildly positive. The shares are 9.3 pp ahead of SPY over the last 126 trading days but still 27.1% below their 52-week high.
key_risks: Revenue is slipping, with a latest-quarter revenue decline of 4.0% year on year and growth slowing.
Apple's known shift away from Qualcomm modems weighs on handset revenue.
The bet on non-handset and Data Center growth may not deliver the targets management set out in July.
The outcome of the Arm licensing dispute is uncertain; a pending ruling on royalties could be worth about $1.5 billion.
EV/EBIT is more expensive than at 43 of the last 61 month-ends, which leaves little room if results disappoint.
what_would_change: A move to Buy needs 9 more points, most plausibly from a growth score recovery if the Q4 FY26 results on November 4 show revenue turning back up.
A cheaper valuation or stronger price trend toward the 52-week high would also help lift the score.
A drop to Sell would need a fall of 12 points, for example from further revenue declines, margin erosion or a negative turn in guidance or litigation news.
